fields.meta_title: Model Release Form Builder for Shoots and Stock | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a model release form that records which uses each model agreed to and flags any frame shot without a signed release. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Model Release Form Tied to the Frames It Covers
fields.hero_description: Describe the shoot and the uses you need. Emergent builds a model release form the model signs on set, then files each signed release beside its frames in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What a Model Release Has to Pin Down
fields.features_subheading: A release earns its keep a year later, when a client asks whether one frame can run in a new campaign.
fields.feature_1:
Usage rights granted line by line

List each use you may need, such as packaging or paid social, with a term and a territory. The model grants them one at a time, and every answer is saved as a field you can query.
fields.feature_2:
Fee and term on the record

Record what the model receives, whether a cash fee or a set of edited images, plus the date the license ends. Anyone checking an old frame sees the terms without hunting for a PDF.
fields.feature_3:
Guardian signatures for minors

Ask for the model's date of birth before anything else. A model under 18 is routed to a page the parent or guardian completes, and both names are saved on the same release.
fields.feature_4:
Releases matched to frames

Give every release a shoot number, then tag frames with it as they come off the memory card. Any frame that shows a person with no matching release is flagged before export.
fields.feature_5:
Extended releases on request

Send a model a new release when a client wants a use the first one left out. Their answer updates the record, and the photographer gets an email the moment it comes back signed.
fields.feature_6:
Your code, on your GitHub

Export the full source of the release app and its database to your GitHub. A developer can host it on your own servers or connect it to the studio software you already run.

fields.tab_content_1:
A signed release before any shutter clicks

Dana Reyes books a model for a skincare shoot for Lumen Botanics. Jordan Hale signs on her phone at the studio while the lights are set up. The release records a $300 fee and a 2-year term. It also carries shoot number S-0412, and every frame from the session is filed under that number.
fields.tab_content_2:
7 frames with no release stay off the upload

Stock agencies turn away images of a recognizable person without a signed release. Before Dana uploads her Harbor Market set, her submission list checks it against her releases: 7 of the 40 frames show a stallholder who never signed. Those are held back, and the other 33 go to the upload queue.
fields.tab_content_3:
8 of 9 cast signed by call time

Call time is 7:00 AM for a Globex product video with 9 cast members. Each one signs a talent release on the producer's tablet at check-in. At 6:30 AM the producer gets a Slack message: 8 of 9 signed. The one missing is Leo, 14, whose guardian is still on the way.
fields.tab_content_4:
A portfolio release meets an ad request

Trade shoots carry narrow releases. Maya Ortiz modeled for Dana's portfolio with no fee and portfolio use only. When Initech asks to run frame 0214 in a paid ad, the image record shows that limit. Dana sends Maya an extended release with a $450 fee, and the frame stays locked until she signs.

fields.howto_title: How to Write a Model Release Form
fields.howto_description: Settle the uses and the money before you write a word. The rest of the release follows from those two decisions.
fields.howto_step_1_des: Decide which uses the release grants before drafting anything. Client work usually needs advertising and packaging rights, while a portfolio shoot may need only your site and print book. Set a term in years and say whether the rights hold worldwide.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Name the parties in full: the photographer or studio, the model and the paying client if there is one. Add the shoot date and location so the release can be matched to its frames years later.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write down what the model receives in exchange for the rights. A cash fee is the common case. Trade shoots pay in edited images instead, and the release should say so plainly, along with the date the model gets them.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Ask for date of birth before the signature. Adobe Stock wants a parent or legal guardian to sign for anyone under 18 when the image was made. Collect the guardian's name and relationship on the same release as the child's details.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste your release wording into the prompt with the uses, the fee field and the age rule. Emergent builds the form and the database behind it. Ask it to tag frames with the shoot number, and change any part later by prompting.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Ask Emergent to flag frames whose people have no release on file. Have the producer's Slack get a count of signed releases before call time. Email the photographer whenever an extended release comes back signed.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Run a test release as a 16-year-old model with a guardian. Decline paid social, sign, then open the record and confirm the frame shows that limit. Have a lawyer read the wording before the first real model signs.

plan.angle: The top 10 is downloadable paper: eSign, Cineview and LawDepot PDFs, an RPS sample, StudioBinder's template, a Reddit thread and Fillout's template. They give the wording and stop at the signature. Working photographers and producers lose time afterward: matching a signed release to the frames it covers, proving a stock agency has a release for every recognizable face, getting every cast member and guardian signed before the call time, and checking a portfolio-only release before an image goes into a paid ad. This page explains what goes in a model release and shows it as a working app that ties each release to the shoot, the frames and the uses the model agreed to.

claims_to_source: A model release is signed by the subject of a photograph granting permission to publish it; no release is needed to take the photograph, and publishing an identifiable person's photo that implies endorsement without one can result in civil liability
Adobe Stock requires a signed model release for content that shows a recognizable person, one release per person
Adobe Stock requires a parent or legal guardian to sign the release when the model was under 18 when the content was created
Adobe Stock licenses unreleased editorial content for editorial use only, not to sell or promote a product
A talent release form gives a filmmaker permission to use a person's image, voice or performance in their work
A location release form is signed by a property owner and grants permission to film or photograph on that property
